To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a fault-tolerant method based on planarly constructed 2-dimensional fault blocks is proposed for k-n meshes/tori, and the method improves the performance of fault-tolerant methods greatly.

a new concept, called "extended local safety information" in meshes/tori, is proposed to enhance fault-tolerant routings, and many nodes globally marked as "unsafe" become "locally enabled" inside 2-dimensional fault blocks.
our method does not need the disabling of any fault-free node and does not need to use a large number of fault-free nodes for constructing fault blocks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
fault-tolerant communication in meshes/tori, and the results can be applied in many fields such as parallel computing and interconnection networks.
the design and analysis of efficient and scalable algorithms to route messages in a network with faults.
the design and analysis of fault-tolerant algorithms for k-ary meshes/tori.

our method is the best one in terms of the number of disabled nodes, the number of faulty nodes and the number of disabled links.
the new routing algorithm is superior to all previous methods in terms of the number of disabled nodes, the number of blocked messages, and the average number of message hops.
our method is the most efficient and effective method for fault-tolerance in meshes/tori.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our method improves the performance of routing algorithm greatly and does not need to waste computational resources to disable any faultfree nodes.
the new concept of extended local safety information can make a network safe for fault-tolerent routing even when a few faulty nodes make the whole system unsafe.
the new concept and the routing algorithm based on the concept can improve performance and reliability of the whole system greatly.

the proposed routing algorithm is more efficient than previous methods in terms of performance and fault-tolerant capability.

, by using a simple and efficient method, we can construct fault blocks in the whole system in a planar way, so that we can use a simple and efficient fault-tolerant method to route messages through the whole system.
